text:
maria: Heads-up — since the kernel bump last night about 03:20 UTC, a subset of multi-GPU training jobs on g5p-pool-2 have been failing with NCCL/IB errors. Seen on both EU and us-west racks.

sam: which error messages?

maria: primary log from a failed job: 
```
[0] NCCL WARN Call to ibv_post_send failed: Invalid argument (22)
[0] NCCL WARN net/ib : error posting send, retrying
[0] NCCL INFO Transport "ib" : fallback to "tcp" on rank 2
[0] NCCL ERROR Unhandled ibv_reg_mr failure: sg_list size mismatch
```

jen: sg_list size mismatch? that sounds like a zero-copy scatter-gather list issue in the RDMA path — maybe mlx5 driver change?

kyung: I saw a similar symptom when the NIC firmware had an unexpected sglist limit, caused zero-copy registrations to fail and the stack fall back to tcp (huge perf hit). Did we roll NIC firmware or driver?

maria: We rolled the 5.19->6.1 kernel and updated mlx5_core last night as part of the security backport. No explicit NIC FW change but driver behavior could differ.

ops-bot: Deployment note: kernel-upgrade-2026-03-17 applied to rack eu-west-3 / us-west-1 at 03:12 UTC (change-id: CU-8823).

sam: Can someone run `ibv_devinfo -v` and `ethtool -k <iface>` on a problematic host? Also `dmesg | grep mlx5` and `grep -i sg /sys/module/mlx5_core/parameters/*` if present.

maria: quick dump attached (pasted): 
```
$ ibv_devinfo -v
hca_id: mlx5_0
transport: InfiniBand (0)
firmware_version: 16.28.1234
max_sge_recv: 30
max_sge_send: 4
max_sge_inline_recv: 0
...
$ cat /sys/module/mlx5_core/parameters/sg_list_max
4
$ dmesg | tail -n 20
mlx5_core: sglist: enforced max 4, attempted 8, rejecting MR registration
```

kyung: that `sglist` param is the smoking gun — kernel/driver now enforces a lower sglist count (4), but NCCL/GPUDirect expects larger scatter-gather entries for zero-copy.

jen: Workarounds? increase sglist or force NCCL to not use ib?

sam: Two short paths: A) bump kernel/driver param to allow larger sglist (risky on stable fleet until validated) — sysctl/module param if exposed; B) set env to force NCCL to avoid IB transport for affected jobs: `export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (will fall back to TCP and cause perf regression but keep jobs alive).

maria: I tested export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 in a staging job and it completes. Perf penalty ~4x for all-reduce on 8xA100 equivalent. For urgent customer runs we can temporarily set job env in the scheduler.

oncall-alex: For immediate mitigation I can roll a scheduler hook to inject `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` into new jobs in g5p-pool-2 and drain+recycle nodes for a safe reboot. Want approval?

sam: do it for a limited window and only in impacted racks. Also create a gate so high-SLA customers can opt-in to wait for a proper fix.

jen: Long-term fix: vendor driver/firmware or revert the kernel patch that reduced sglist, or adapt NCCL/GPUDirect to use fewer sges (probably harder). We should open a support ticket with Mellanox/Driver team, include `dmesg`, `ibv_devinfo`, exact kernel version and failing workload trace.

maria: Filed internal ticket INFRA-6129 + opened vendor case with attached logs (case MLX-8392). Linking here.

ops-bot: INFRA-6129 created by maria at 2026-03-17T04:10:23Z.

kyung: Also check if jumbo MTU or VXLAN offload spins up fragmentation that increases sge count in DPDK/skb scatter — edge case but seen before.

maria: Good call — our ToR had an MTU mismatch in one of the aggregation switches (1500 vs 9000) after a config drift on 03/16. I've opened a sibling ticket for config sync. Might explain why some racks more affected.

sam: Plan suggested: 1) immediate: add `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` gate and drain affected hosts (oncall-alex). 2) medium: vendor driver follow-up + test matrix on kernel 6.1 variants (eng-ml + eng-infra). 3) long: validate ToR MTU and offload settings cluster-wide and reconcile config drift scripts.

maria: rolling the env injection now for eu-west-3, monitoring. Will update when we see new failures.

oncall-alex: done — gate applied to g5p-pool-2 (eu-west-3) at 04:25 UTC, draining 6 nodes, patch ID GC-2026-03-17-01.

maria: after gate, jobs that previously failed now progressing (still slow) — no immediate new ibv_reg_mr errors in logs.

sam: thanks. keep the vendor case updated and schedule a driver rollback test on a canary rack before mass roll.

jen: adding a short runbook snippet to INFRA-6129 with commands: 
```
# Check sglist cap
cat /sys/module/mlx5_core/parameters/sg_list_max
# Temp workaround for job via scheduler (slurm example):
srun --job-name=train -x kube-node-1 -e NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 python train.py
```

maria: thumbs up. I'll follow up with a postmortem once vendor confirms root cause. :thumbsup:

sam: cool — tag me on the postmortem.

jen: noted. thanks everyone.
